implication: A Reg 31(4) disclosure signals that a threshold shareholding event (typically 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 50%, or 75%) has been triggered requiring immediate regulatory notification; practitioners must review the full disclosure document to identify the acquirer, percentage stake, and any consequent open offer or exemption claim.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of acquisition of shares/voting rights that triggers Code obligations (typically ≥5% of voting capital); filing must be made within 2 business days of crossing threshold.
Defines 'Acquirer' and threshold events (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 50%, 75%) that trigger open offer or exemption claims.
Exemptions from open offer for acquisitions made in good faith, to comply with court orders, or by Government/specified entities.
Deposit of shares in abeyance if beneficial ownership unclear; relevant to acquisition settlement mechanics.
Dematerialisation and beneficial ownership records; central to stake verification in listed company acquisitions.
Open Offer terms: minimum offer price, quantity, timing, and shareholder eligibility if threshold triggered and exemption not claimed.
If acquisition involves any derivatives, futures or paired trades, anti-fraud provisions apply; review if stake buildup preceded formal acquisition.
